findings.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime keys: the audit-logs endpoint paginates on datetime, and math.floor/math.ceil on a datetime raises TypeError, so every optimized_pagination=true request against an org with at least one audit entry returns a 500 on page 1 (the class copied BasicPaginator's numeric key handling instead of DateTimePaginator's datetime handling)

value_from_cursor doesn't convert the serialized cursor value back to a datetime before it's used in build_queryset (unlike DateTimePaginator's override), so a cursor-following request would filter datetime__lt=<raw int/str> and fail with a validation/DB error

Negative-offset slicing raises Django's AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') because Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing — the comment claiming the ORM handles it automatically is factually wrong, so the advanced feature can never execute successfully and a hand-crafted negative-offset cursor causes a 500

organization_context.member.has_global_access is evaluated unconditionally on every GET (outside the use_optimized check) with no None-guard: the attribute chain may not exist on ControlSiloOrganizationEndpoint/OrganizationMember, and member is None for requesters permitted by OrganizationAuditPermission without a membership row (e.g. staff-mode users), potentially turning the entire audit-logs endpoint into a 500 for all clients

Base get_result silently masks invalid forward cursors via max(0, offset), rewriting a negative/corrupt cursor offset to 0 and returning a 200 with page-1 data instead of failing loudly, while prev cursors with the same invalid input still pass through unclamped and hit the negative-slicing AssertionError — inconsistent behavior for the same invalid condition, applied to every cursor-paginated endpoint via the shared BasePaginator
The optimized path issues identical queries to the default path (same queryset, same slice window), so the PR adds crash surface with no actual performance gain

`organization_context` is undefined in `src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71` — `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally before the `use_optimized` check, but `organization_context` is never defined, causing a NameError and 500 on every GET of the audit-logs endpoint for all users

Negative-offset slicing in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (`src/sentry/api/paginator.py:876-881`) raises an error — Django QuerySets do not support negative slice bounds, so any caller sending a negative-offset cursor with `optimized_pagination=true` gets a guaranteed 500; the comments falsely claim the ORM handles negative slicing and boundary conditions automatically

`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` (`src/sentry/api/paginator.py:837-839`) is incompatible with the endpoint's datetime sort key — `math.floor(value)` raises TypeError when `build_cursor` calls `key(results[-1])` on any page containing rows since `value` is a datetime; datetime cursor values also lack conversion in `value_from_cursor` (lines 841-842), and `build_queryset`/`_is_asc`/`key` may not exist on a direct `BasePaginator` subclass since they live on `CursorPaginator`

`OffsetPaginator.get_result` (`src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-184`) is a no-op for valid input and silently returns wrong results for forged input — `max(0, offset)` never changes behavior for legitimate cursors (no performance improvement), while crafted negative-offset forward cursors are silently clamped to offset 0, returning the dataset's first page as the client's current position, and prev cursors still crash on `queryset[negative:...]`; this affects every offset-paginated endpoint sharing the base class

The advertised optimization does not exist — the optimized branch performs the same queryset slice (bounded by `max_limit`), same serialization, and same hits counting as the default path, eliminating no queries and reducing no rows read, so the PR adds crash paths and risk with zero performance payoff while the title and comments misrepresent this

The endpoint exposes two incompatible cursor contracts selected by a magic param and the caller's role (`src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70-88`) — cursors emitted with `optimized_pagination=true` use a different value encoding than default mode, so cursors are not interchangeable across modes or across a user's role change, breaking pagination for clients that persist or replay cursors

In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71, `organization_context` is never defined (and `OrganizationMember` does not expose `has_global_access`; global-access checks live on `request.access`), so the unconditionally executed line `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises NameError and hard-500s GET /api/0/organizations/<slug>/audit-logs/ for every non-superuser request, flag or no flag.

OptimizedCursorPaginator (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840, 843) implements a numeric-key contract but is wired to a datetime-ordered endpoint (order_by="-datetime"): get_item_key applies int(math.floor(value)) to a datetime, raising TypeError on any full page (len(results) > limit), and value_from_cursor returns a raw int that build_queryset uses to filter datetime__lt=<int>, which Django rejects — so the optimized path 500s on its first real invocation and the feature is dead on arrival.

In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877-882, the negative-offset "advanced feature" crashes because Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing (QuerySet.__getitem__ raises AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported), and for sequence-backed paginators Python negative indexing would silently return a window anchored to the end of the data — the branch can never function as written despite the comment claiming the ORM handles it.

Unversioned behavior change to BasePaginator.get_result (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184), the base class shared by every cursor-paginated endpoint: a forged forward cursor with a negative offset, which previously failed fast with Django AssertionError, is now silently clamped to offset 0 and returns a wrong page, while a forged prev cursor with the same negative offset still crashes — inconsistent handling of identical invalid input with no legitimate benefit, since server-generated cursors never carry negative offsets and the stated bidirectional-pagination justification describes a capability that doesn't exist.

The new undocumented `optimized_pagination` flag (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70-83) forks the cursor contract of an existing public route with behavior varying by user identity: DateTimePaginator emits/decodes epoch-second values while OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor consumes the raw value, so a client that toggles the flag or whose admin status changes mid-pagination feeds a cursor from one format into the other, producing errors or wrong windows — response-contract drift with no docs, no versioning, no caller consideration, and a false docstring claim of backward compatibility.

organization_auditlogs.py:71: `organization_context` is not defined in `get()`'s scope, so any non-superuser sending `?optimized_pagination=true` triggers a `NameError` → 500; because `or` short-circuits, superusers never evaluate it, so superuser-fixture tests pass CI while real org admins crash
organization_auditlogs.py:71: even if `organization_context` existed, `.member` can be `None`, causing an `AttributeError`

organization_auditlogs.py:82: `enable_advanced_features=True` is forwarded into `sentry.api.paginator.paginate()`, whose fixed signature does not accept it, causing a `TypeError` → 500 whenever the optimized branch runs

Even if `paginate()` tolerated the `enable_advanced_features` kwarg, it constructs the paginator without forwarding it, so `self.enable_advanced_features` would silently stay `False` and the advertised advanced features are dead code

paginator.py:837-839: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` to a datetime value, raising a `TypeError`; `build_cursor` calls the key whenever a page returns more than `limit` rows, so the first page 500s for any org with more than one page of audit entries

paginator.py:841-842: `value_from_cursor` returns the raw int instead of converting it to a datetime, so `filter(datetime__lt=<int>)` against a DateTimeField raises a Django `ValidationError` → 500 for any cursor with a non-zero value
paginator.py:841-842: when the cursor value stays 0, pagination silently degrades to pure offset scanning with no key predicate — the opposite of an optimization

paginator.py:876-881: the negative-offset branch calls `list(queryset[-N:...])` on a Django QuerySet, which raises `AssertionError('Negative indexes are not supported')` — the ORM does not properly handle negative slicing, so a crafted negative-offset cursor produces a 500
paginator.py:876-881: if a caller passes a list/evaluated sequence instead of a QuerySet, negative slicing reads from the end of the dataset, allowing access to data beyond normal pagination bounds

The safety comments ('the ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level') are false — no permission check was added and offset handling is unrelated to queryset scoping; they assert safety the code does not provide

paginator.py:182-184: `BasePaginator.get_result` now silently clamps forward cursors with negative offsets to offset 0 and returns data where the old code failed loudly with `AssertionError`, while prev cursors with negative offsets still crash — an inconsistent, mislabeled clamp that changes malformed-cursor behavior for every OffsetPaginator/DateTimePaginator endpoint in the API for zero benefit

cursors.py:24-25: comment-only change claims negative offsets are now 'allowed', but `int(offset)` always parsed any int, so it changes nothing and only makes the negative-offset narrative look deliberate across files

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and uses it for `organization_auditlogs` with `order_by="-datetime"`. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, it derives `cursor_value = self.value_from_cursor(cursor)` and passes that into `self.build_queryset(cursor_value, cursor.is_prev)`, but `value_from_cursor` is implemented as `return cursor.value` with no conversion. Given this paginator is being applied to a datetime-ordered queryset, passing the raw serialized cursor value into `build_queryset` risks producing datetime comparisons against an unparsed string/int cursor value (i.e., the type mismatch the finding describes). The diff itself shows the lack of conversion and the datetime usage at the callsite.

Base get_result silently masks invalid forward cursors via max(0, offset), rewriting a negative/corrupt cursor offset to 0 and returning a 200 with page-1 data instead of failing loudly, while prev cursors with the same invalid input still pass through unclamped and hit the negative-slicing AssertionError — inconsistent behavior for the same invalid condition, applied to every cursor-paginated endpoint via the shared BasePaginator

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py:get_result`, the diff changes slicing to use `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, which clamps negative offsets only for forward pagination but allows negative offsets through when `cursor.is_prev` is true. Since cursor offsets originate from `Cursor.offset = int(offset)` (`src/sentry/utils/cursors.py`) and can be user-controlled/corrupt, this introduces inconsistent behavior: forward cursors with negative offsets are silently rewritten to 0 (returning first-page data), while prev cursors with the same negative offset will attempt `queryset[offset:stop]` with a negative start, which Django QuerySet slicing typically rejects (raising an AssertionError). This inconsistent handling and potential 500 for `is_prev` is a concrete correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The optimized path issues identical queries to the default path (same queryset, same slice window), so the PR adds crash surface with no actual performance gain

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the “optimized” branch passes the same `queryset` and `order_by="-datetime"` to `self.paginate` as the default branch; the only visible behavioral change is swapping `DateTimePaginator` for the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and enabling `enable_advanced_features=True`. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the main path (when `cursor.offset >= 0`) computes `start_offset`/`stop` and slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` the same way as the updated existing paginator logic, so for typical non-negative offsets it will issue an equivalent slice query. This makes the reviewer’s point (added complexity/crash surface with no clear diff-grounded performance win) a concrete, diff-based concern, though “no actual performance gain” can’t be fully proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `organization_context` is undefined in `src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71` — `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally before the `use_optimized` check, but `organization_context` is never defined, causing a NameError and 500 on every GET of the audit-logs endpoint for all users

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new line `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` references `organization_context`, but the diff shows no local definition or import for that name in the surrounding code. Since this expression is evaluated before the `if use_optimized and enable_advanced:` branch, an undefined `organization_context` would raise a `NameError` during every GET request to this endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Negative-offset slicing in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (`src/sentry/api/paginator.py:876-881`) raises an error — Django QuerySets do not support negative slice bounds, so any caller sending a negative-offset cursor with `optimized_pagination=true` gets a guaranteed 500; the comments falsely claim the ORM handles negative slicing and boundary conditions automatically

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces negative-offset slicing in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0` (`start_offset = cursor.offset` then `queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django QuerySets do not support negative slice bounds (negative indexing/slicing raises an error), so a request supplying a cursor with a negative offset under `optimized_pagination=true` can trigger a server error. The surrounding comments claiming the ORM “properly handles negative slicing automatically” are not supported by Django behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` (`src/sentry/api/paginator.py:837-839`) is incompatible with the endpoint's datetime sort key — `math.floor(value)` raises TypeError when `build_cursor` calls `key(results[-1])` on any page containing rows since `value` is a datetime; datetime cursor values also lack conversion in `value_from_cursor` (lines 841-842), and `build_queryset`/`_is_asc`/`key` may not exist on a direct `BasePaginator` subclass since they live on `CursorPaginator`

adjudication.rationale: The endpoint switches to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while still ordering by `-datetime` (`organization_auditlogs.py`), so the paginator’s key will be the datetime field. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key`, it does `math.floor(value)`/`math.ceil(value)` on `value = getattr(item, self.key)`, which will raise `TypeError` if `value` is a `datetime` (not a number). Additionally, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` subclasses `BasePaginator` but its `get_result` calls cursor-paginator-specific APIs/attrs like `build_queryset`, `_is_asc`, `desc`, and `post_query_filter` that are not defined in this diff, making runtime failure likely if `BasePaginator` doesn’t provide them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `OffsetPaginator.get_result` (`src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-184`) is a no-op for valid input and silently returns wrong results for forged input — `max(0, offset)` never changes behavior for legitimate cursors (no performance improvement), while crafted negative-offset forward cursors are silently clamped to offset 0, returning the dataset's first page as the client's current position, and prev cursors still crash on `queryset[negative:...]`; this affects every offset-paginated endpoint sharing the base class

adjudication.rationale: In `OffsetPaginator.get_result`, the diff changes slicing from `queryset[offset:stop]` to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset = max(0, offset)` for non-prev cursors. For legitimate cursors with non-negative `offset`, this is effectively a no-op; for forged negative `offset` with `cursor.is_prev == False`, it silently clamps to `0` and returns the first page rather than rejecting/raising, changing behavior and yielding incorrect pagination results. Additionally, for `cursor.is_prev == True`, the code still uses `offset` directly (`start_offset = offset`), so a negative offset can still lead to a negative queryset slice, which Django `QuerySet` slicing typically does not support and can raise (i.e., potential crash). This impacts all endpoints using this paginator code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The advertised optimization does not exist — the optimized branch performs the same queryset slice (bounded by `max_limit`), same serialization, and same hits counting as the default path, eliminating no queries and reducing no rows read, so the PR adds crash paths and risk with zero performance payoff while the title and comments misrepresent this

adjudication.rationale: From the diff, the “optimized” path largely mirrors the default pagination behavior: it still clamps `limit` by `self.max_limit`, still does a Django slice `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, and still uses the same `on_results=lambda x: serialize(x, request.user)` with the same hit-counting flow (`count_hits/known_hits` logic is unchanged inside the new paginator). The only clearly new behavior is optional negative-offset handling when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, but nothing in the endpoint shows that such cursors are produced/used in normal operation. So the finding that the PR adds complexity/risk without a verifiable performance win is grounded, though “zero payoff” is a bit stronger than what can be strictly proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The endpoint exposes two incompatible cursor contracts selected by a magic param and the caller's role (`src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70-88`) — cursors emitted with `optimized_pagination=true` use a different value encoding than default mode, so cursors are not interchangeable across modes or across a user's role change, breaking pagination for clients that persist or replay cursors

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes pagination behavior (and therefore cursor generation/interpretation) conditional on a magic query param and the caller’s privileges: `optimized_pagination=true` + `is_superuser or ...has_global_access` switches from `DateTimePaginator` to the newly added `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (`organization_auditlogs.py`), otherwise it stays on `DateTimePaginator`. Since these are different paginator implementations and `OptimizedCursorPaginator` computes cursor values via its own `get_item_key` (int floor/ceil of the item attribute) and has different offset handling, cursors emitted in one mode are not guaranteed to be accepted/meaningful in the other. That means a client persisting/replaying cursors can break when toggling the param or when a user’s role changes and the endpoint silently changes paginator class.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71, `organization_context` is never defined (and `OrganizationMember` does not expose `has_global_access`; global-access checks live on `request.access`), so the unconditionally executed line `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises NameError and hard-500s GET /api/0/organizations/<slug>/audit-logs/ for every non-superuser request, flag or no flag.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` inside `get()`. In the shown hunk, `organization_context` is not defined anywhere before this use, and the assignment executes for every request (only short-circuiting for superusers). If `organization_context` is indeed not defined elsewhere in the function/file, this will raise `NameError` for non-superuser requests regardless of the `optimized_pagination` flag.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840, 843) implements a numeric-key contract but is wired to a datetime-ordered endpoint (order_by="-datetime"): get_item_key applies int(math.floor(value)) to a datetime, raising TypeError on any full page (len(results) > limit), and value_from_cursor returns a raw int that build_queryset uses to filter datetime__lt=<int>, which Django rejects — so the optimized path 500s on its first real invocation and the feature is dead on arrival.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the optimized path switches to `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` while still paginating with `order_by="-datetime"`. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` assumes the paginator key field is numeric (`int(math.floor(value))` / `math.ceil(value)`), but if the paginator key is `datetime` (as implied by the endpoint ordering), `value` would be a `datetime` object and `math.floor/ceil` will raise `TypeError`. Additionally, `value_from_cursor()` returns the cursor value unchanged, so if `build_queryset()` (inherited from `BasePaginator`) uses that value in comparisons on the `datetime` field, it would be comparing a datetime field to an int, which Django will reject. The diff shows no datetime-specific handling in `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, so wiring it to a datetime-ordered endpoint is very likely to break at runtime when the optimized flag is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877-882, the negative-offset "advanced feature" crashes because Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing (QuerySet.__getitem__ raises AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported), and for sequence-backed paginators Python negative indexing would silently return a window anchored to the end of the data — the branch can never function as written despite the comment claiming the ORM handles it.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result()` adds a branch that intentionally slices a Django `QuerySet` with a negative start (`start_offset = cursor.offset` when `cursor.offset < 0`) and then does `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django `QuerySet.__getitem__` does not support negative indexing/slicing and will raise an `AssertionError` for negative indices, so this “advanced feature” path cannot work as written despite the comment claiming the ORM handles it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unversioned behavior change to BasePaginator.get_result (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184), the base class shared by every cursor-paginated endpoint: a forged forward cursor with a negative offset, which previously failed fast with Django AssertionError, is now silently clamped to offset 0 and returns a wrong page, while a forged prev cursor with the same negative offset still crashes — inconsistent handling of identical invalid input with no legitimate benefit, since server-generated cursors never carry negative offsets and the stated bidirectional-pagination justification describes a capability that doesn't exist.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `BasePaginator.get_result` slicing from `queryset[offset:stop]` to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. This clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward pagination but leaves negative offsets unchanged for `is_prev`, which can still hit Django's negative-slice assertion. That is an unversioned behavior change: invalid negative `cursor.offset` now silently returns the first page for forward cursors (wrong page) while still erroring for prev cursors—an inconsistent, correctness-affecting handling of the same invalid input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new undocumented `optimized_pagination` flag (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70-83) forks the cursor contract of an existing public route with behavior varying by user identity: DateTimePaginator emits/decodes epoch-second values while OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor consumes the raw value, so a client that toggles the flag or whose admin status changes mid-pagination feeds a cursor from one format into the other, producing errors or wrong windows — response-contract drift with no docs, no versioning, no caller consideration, and a false docstring claim of backward compatibility.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces an `optimized_pagination` query flag that switches the endpoint between `DateTimePaginator` and the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` based on both request params and user/org privileges (organization_auditlogs.py). That means the same public route can emit different cursor behavior depending on caller identity/flag, and nothing in the diff shows any negotiation/versioning to ensure clients don’t accidentally reuse a cursor across modes. However, the finding’s specific claim that `DateTimePaginator` uses epoch-second cursor values while `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` consumes a raw value is not verifiable from this diff because `DateTimePaginator`’s encoding/decoding is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organization_auditlogs.py:71: `organization_context` is not defined in `get()`'s scope, so any non-superuser sending `?optimized_pagination=true` triggers a `NameError` → 500; because `or` short-circuits, superusers never evaluate it, so superuser-fixture tests pass CI while real org admins crash

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` in `organization_auditlogs.py` without showing any definition of `organization_context` in the displayed scope. If `organization_context` is not provided as a `get()` parameter or set earlier in the method, this will raise a `NameError` for non-superusers when `optimized_pagination=true` is used (superusers short-circuit the `or`). This is a concrete runtime failure risk introduced by the change, though the diff excerpt doesn’t fully prove `organization_context` isn’t defined elsewhere in `get()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: paginator.py:837-839: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` to a datetime value, raising a `TypeError`; `build_cursor` calls the key whenever a page returns more than `limit` rows, so the first page 500s for any org with more than one page of audit entries

In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the optimized path paginates audit log entries ordered by `-datetime` (`order_by="-datetime"`), so the paginator’s key is very likely the model’s `datetime` field (a `datetime` object). `math.floor`/`math.ceil` do not accept `datetime` values and will raise `TypeError`, breaking pagination whenever `get_item_key` is invoked during cursor construction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: paginator.py:841-842: `value_from_cursor` returns the raw int instead of converting it to a datetime, so `filter(datetime__lt=<int>)` against a DateTimeField raises a Django `ValidationError` → 500 for any cursor with a non-zero value

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and the audit log endpoint can select it while ordering by `-datetime` (a `DateTimeField`). In `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, `value_from_cursor()` returns `cursor.value` unchanged, and `get_item_key()` applies `math.floor/ceil` to `getattr(item, self.key)`, which for `datetime` would not be numeric. Given `BasePaginator.build_queryset()` typically uses the cursor value to filter on the ordering key, using a raw int cursor value for a datetime-ordered queryset is very likely to produce invalid ORM filters (e.g., `datetime__lt=<int>`) or type errors, resulting in 500s when a non-zero cursor is used.

The claim about silent degradation to pure offset scanning cannot be confirmed from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: paginator.py:876-881: the negative-offset branch calls `list(queryset[-N:...])` on a Django QuerySet, which raises `AssertionError('Negative indexes are not supported')` — the ORM does not properly handle negative slicing, so a crafted negative-offset cursor produces a 500

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the branch `if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0:` sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. The diff’s own comments claim Django ORM handles negative slicing, but Django `QuerySet` slicing with a negative index is not supported and raises an `AssertionError` (negative indexes not supported). Since `Cursor.offset` is taken directly from the cursor (`self.offset = int(offset)` in `cursors.py`), a crafted negative offset can trigger a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: paginator.py:876-881: if a caller passes a list/evaluated sequence instead of a QuerySet, negative slicing reads from the end of the dataset, allowing access to data beyond normal pagination bounds

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then slices `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`. The diff does not enforce that `queryset` is a Django `QuerySet`; if a caller passes an already-evaluated sequence (e.g., a `list`), negative slice starts read from the end of the sequence, which can return items outside the intended forward-pagination window (i.e., “beyond normal pagination bounds”). This behavior is directly enabled by the new negative-offset path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The safety comments ('the ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level') are false — no permission check was added and offset handling is unrelated to queryset scoping; they assert safety the code does not provide

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds comments asserting safety based on (a) “permissions are checked at the queryset level” and (b) “the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically” (see `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` and the modified `get_result` earlier). However, this PR does not add any new permission checks or queryset scoping tied to offset handling—`enable_advanced` is only used to gate feature flags, not to enforce authorization beyond existing endpoint logic—so the comment about permissions is not supported by the shown changes. Independently, the ORM/negative-slicing claim is also not substantiated anywhere in the diff (it’s just a comment), making the safety rationale misleading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: paginator.py:182-184: `BasePaginator.get_result` now silently clamps forward cursors with negative offsets to offset 0 and returns data where the old code failed loudly with `AssertionError`, while prev cursors with negative offsets still crash — an inconsistent, mislabeled clamp that changes malformed-cursor behavior for every OffsetPaginator/DateTimePaginator endpoint in the API for zero benefit

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `BasePaginator.get_result` from `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` to computing `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` and slicing `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. This means a negative `cursor.offset` for a forward cursor is silently clamped to 0 (returning the first page) while a negative offset for a prev cursor is still passed through and will hit Django queryset negative-slice assertions. That is an inconsistent behavior change affecting all endpoints using `BasePaginator`-based paginators (e.g., `DateTimePaginator`) and can mask malformed cursors by returning unexpected data instead of erroring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cursors.py:24-25: comment-only change claims negative offsets are now 'allowed', but `int(offset)` always parsed any int, so it changes nothing and only makes the negative-offset narrative look deliberate across files

adjudication.rationale: In `cursors.py` the only change is adding comments above `self.offset = int(offset)`. The assignment already accepted negative integers before (via `int(offset)`), so the finding that this change “changes nothing” is accurate, but it’s essentially a documentation/style nit rather than an important review issue grounded in functional behavior. The diff’s actual behavior changes around offsets happen in the paginator code, not in `Cursor.__init__`.
